import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_40/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_40/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length5_40/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source0 and Source1 on Cust_id
# Cust_id in source0 is like 'Cust_1', in source1 also 'Cust_1', so join on exact string match
df_01 = pd.merge(source1, source0[['Customer_Name', 'Cust_id']], on='Cust_id', how='inner')

# Step 2: Join the result with Source4 on Ship_id
df_final = pd.merge(df_01, source4[['Ship_id']], on='Ship_id', how='inner')

# Now, transform columns to match target schema and types:
# Target schema: ['Ship_id': string, 'Customer_Name': string, 'Ord_id': integer, 'Prod_id': integer, 'Cust_id': integer]

# Convert Cust_id from 'Cust_XXX' to integer XXX
df_final['Cust_id'] = df_final['Cust_id'].str.replace('Cust_', '').astype(int)

# Convert Ord_id from 'Ord_XXX' to integer XXX
df_final['Ord_id'] = df_final['Ord_id'].str.replace('Ord_', '').astype(int)

# Convert Prod_id from 'Prod_XXX' to integer XXX
df_final['Prod_id'] = df_final['Prod_id'].str.replace('Prod_', '').astype(int)

# Ship_id and Customer_Name remain as string, no change needed

# Select only the target columns in the correct order
target_df = df_final[['Ship_id', 'Customer_Name', 'Ord_id', 'Prod_id', 'Cust_id']]

# Write the result to the specified path without the index
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_40/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_40/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_40/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_40/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_40/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_40/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source5_40_0 and Source5_40_1 on Cust_id
joined_01 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="Cust_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source5_40_2 on Ord_id
joined_01_2 = pd.merge(joined_01, source2, on="Ord_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source5_40_3 on Prod_id
joined_01_3 = pd.merge(joined_01_2, source3, on="Prod_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source5_40_4 on Ship_id
final_join = pd.merge(joined_01_3, source4, on="Ship_id", how="inner")

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema exactly
# Target schema: ['Ship_id': string, 'Customer_Name': string, 'Ord_id': integer, 'Prod_id': integer, 'Cust_id': integer]
# Convert Ord_id, Prod_id, Cust_id to integer by extracting numeric part after underscore

def extract_int_id(col):
    # Extract integer part after underscore, e.g. "Ord_1082" -> 1082
    return col.str.extract(r'_(\d+)$').astype(int)

final_df = pd.DataFrame()
final_df["Ship_id"] = final_join["Ship_id"]
final_df["Customer_Name"] = final_join["Customer_Name"]
final_df["Ord_id"] = extract_int_id(final_join["Ord_id"])
final_df["Prod_id"] = extract_int_id(final_join["Prod_id"])
final_df["Cust_id"] = extract_int_id(final_join["Cust_id"])

# Group by all columns (which are all leftmost non-float unique columns) to remove duplicates if any
final_df = final_df.groupby(["Ship_id", "Customer_Name", "Ord_id", "Prod_id", "Cust_id"], as_index=False).size()
final_df = final_df.drop(columns=["size"])  # size is just count, not needed

# Write to output CSV
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_40/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
